task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! My mobile data has been acting up — it either stops working completely or crawls along really slowly. I'd really like to get it sorted out today. I'm John Smith, by the way, and my number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
Hi John — I've found the issue. On your line **555-123-2002** (line ID L1002, Premium Plan), you've used **15.1 GB out of your 15 GB monthly limit**, so your data has been cut off/slowed for this billing cycle (which ends 2025-02-28).

There are two ways to get you back up and running:

1. **Refuel data** – add extra data right away at **$2.00 per GB** on your Premium Plan (maximum 2 GB, so up to $4.00). This applies immediately and is charged to your bill.
2. **Change to a different plan** with a higher data allowance going forward.

Which would you like to do? If refueling, how many GB would you like me to add (1 or 2 GB at $2.00/GB)?
turns.execution_output:
User: Hmm, that's a bit frustrating to hear — I had no idea I'd gone over my limit. But okay, let's go with the refuel option. Please add the full **2 GB** for me.

One thing I should mention — I'm currently abroad in France, so I'm on roaming. Not sure if that makes a difference to how the refuel works, but thought I'd let you know.

And just to be clear, I'd like to stay on my current Premium Plan — I don't want to change plans.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
I've added the full **2 GB** to your line 555-123-2002 for **$4.00** (at your plan's $2.00/GB rate), charged to your bill. Your line now shows 2.0 GB of refueled data on top of your 15 GB allowance. You're staying on the Premium Plan — no plan change was made.

Regarding roaming: your line L1002 is already roaming-enabled, so you're all set to use the data while you're in France. If mobile data still isn't working on your device, please also make sure that **Data Roaming is turned ON** in your phone's settings (this is a separate switch from the line-level roaming access). Note that roaming isn't needed for the refuel itself — the data applies to your line either way.

Could you check whether your data connection is working now? If it's still slow or not connecting, let me know and I'll help you troubleshoot further (e.g. data saver mode, network mode preference, or VPN settings).
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check on my end.

turns.thought:
Yes — please go ahead and turn both of those on:

1. **Turn Mobile Data ON** in your phone's settings. Since it's off, that alone fully explains the "No Connection" speed test result.
2. **Turn Data Roaming ON** as well. Since you're in France (outside your home network) and your line is roaming-enabled, data roaming needs to be on for the connection to work.

There's one more thing I spotted that will keep things slow even after that: **you're on 2G with poor signal.** 2G isn't really usable for data. Please also change your **network mode preference** to 4G/5G (often listed as "4G/5G preferred" or "LTE/5G auto") in your mobile network settings. That way your phone can connect to a faster network when one is available.

After making those changes, please run the speed test again and let me know the result.

One caveat: the signal showing as "poor" is about your physical reception where you are. If it's still poor after switching modes, try moving somewhere with a clearer view / nearer a window, or connecting to Wi-Fi. If you need calls and texts while the cellular signal is weak, you can also turn on **Wi-Fi Calling** while connected to a Wi-Fi network.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only do one thing at a time on my end, so let me start with the first one — turning mobile data on.

turns.thought:
Good catch — yes, Data Saver can definitely affect your speed. Here's how to handle each one:

1. **Data Saver — turn it OFF.** Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make apps and services feel slow or unresponsive. Please go into your phone's settings and switch it off.

2. **VPN — try disconnecting it as a test.** A VPN encrypts and reroutes your traffic, which can sometimes cause a significant drop in speed. Our guidance is to disconnect it if performance is poor. Since I don't know yet whether it's actually affecting you, I'd suggest: first turn mobile data and data roaming ON and switch your network mode to 4G/5G, then run a speed test. If the result comes back slow, disconnect the VPN and run the speed test again to compare.

I'm not able to change these phone settings remotely, so you'll need to make those changes on your device. Please go ahead with all of the above:

- Mobile Data → ON
- Data Roaming → ON
- Network mode → 4G/5G preferred
- Data Saver → OFF

Then run the speed test and tell me what speed it reports. If it's slow, disconnect the VPN and test again so we can see if it makes a difference.
turns.execution_output: User: Mobile data, roaming, and the network mode are already done from before. Let me turn off Data Saver now.

turns.thought:
Yes, go ahead and try it — since you're at "Good" but still short of "Excellent," the VPN is the remaining thing I can point to. Please disconnect the VPN and run the speed test again to see whether it improves.

Two other things worth checking, since they affect the ceiling on your speed:

- **Did you manage to change your network mode to 4G/5G preferred?** You were on 2G earlier, which would cap you well below excellent speeds even with everything else fixed.
- **Signal strength was "poor."** Roaming speeds depend on the local network's coverage where you are, so a weak signal will limit you regardless of settings. Moving closer to a window or to a more open area can help.

Let me know the new speed test result after disconnecting the VPN, and whether the network mode change took effect.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me disconnect the VPN.
